intended_object: The p-adic Tate module T_p A = lim_n A[p^n] of an abelian group A: the inverse limit of its p^n-torsion subgroups along the multiplication-by-p maps A[p^(n+1)] → A[p^n]. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The carrier is the subgroup `tateModuleSubgroup p A` of the product ∏_n A[p^n]. Here `A[p^n]` is `AddSubgroup.torsionBy A (p^n)`. The subgroup consists of the families (x_n) with p • x_{n+1} = x_n for every n. This is exactly the standard concrete description of the inverse limit lim A[p^n] along multiplication by p, which is the usual definition of the Tate module (Silverman III.7, for example). The level n = 0 is A[1] = 0, which is harmless.

The definition puts no primality condition on `p : ℕ`. It is only needed for the ℤ_p-module structure, and that instance assumes `[Fact p.Prime]` separately, so the bare construction is if anything more general than required. It works for any additive commutative group A, which is the natural generality.

The file also defines the ℤ_p-module structure and the inverse-limit topology, and proves the universal property. All of these match the standard object. Searching Mathlib for "TateModule" and "Tate module" found no counterpart.
